title: The compiler as the framework: what disappears before the browser sees it

videos.script:
Most frameworks send a library to the browser. {{library}} The library reads your components while the page runs, and works out what to change.

Svelte does that work earlier. {{compiler}} It is a compiler. It reads your components on your own computer, before anybody visits, and writes plain JavaScript that changes the page directly. Most of the framework is gone before the browser sees it.

Today you see that happen. {{setup}} First, your computer: Node twenty-two, which you may already have, and a small command called look. It opens a page in a real browser and prints what a screen reader would hear.

Then the project. {{project}} One command makes it, and every lesson after this one changes it. It becomes a study planner: courses, sessions, and the minutes in your week.

Then the part that makes Svelte different. {{compile}} You run the compiler by hand on a component of six lines, and read the two programs it writes. One for the browser. One for the server.

And last, {{build}} you build the project and count what is left for a visitor to download.

One section is about what to do when the setup fails. {{fails}} Read it before you need it.
